mechanism.pieces: The device is software that reads a scanned slide. It returns a clinical call, such as tumour present or a cell count. Selling it needs a European mark or a United States authorisation.
mechanism.normally_wrong: The regulator sees the performance data. The pathologist who must trust the output usually does not. Reviews start from published studies, so a device with no study is invisible to them.
mechanism.what_they_did: They changed the unit of analysis. Instead of reviewing papers, they walked the register of authorised products and asked whether any number exists in public.
mechanism.numbers_mean: The 39 per cent counts devices where a searcher could find evidence in six named sources. It does not show the rest perform badly. Fifteen metrics means two devices usually cannot be ranked.
mechanism.anchor: This is a provenance problem. A validation report published in a fixed, comparable format would already be ahead of most of this market.

glossary.definition: is diagnosis from scanned images of tissue slides.
is the label that lets a product be sold in the European Union.
is a number describing how accurate a test is.

entries.headline: Most approved pathology AI tools have no public evidence of how well they work
body: A team in Helsinki started from the register of authorised devices rather than from the literature. They found 77 AI diagnostic products from 29 manufacturers.
Device specific performance evidence was found in public for 30 of them. For the other 47, which is 61 per cent, nothing could be found at all.
All eight products authorised on both sides of the Atlantic had evidence. Only 22 of 69 European only products did. Fifteen different metrics were used across the publications that exist.
entries.catch: A search based absence is a floor, not a fact. Evidence could sit in a regulatory summary and be missed. Devices were counted, not installations.
entries.simple: Hospitals can buy AI programs that read tissue slides. The programs are legally approved. But for most of them, a doctor cannot find any published test of their accuracy.
entries.why: Ask a vendor for device specific published evidence before anything else. Six times in ten, there will be none to show you.

glossary.definition: is the set of European rules for how medicines are made.
gives outputs that can differ between runs.

entries.headline: Europe's medicines regulator may allow generative models in critical manufacturing
body: The 2025 draft said adaptive and probabilistic models should not be used in critical manufacturing. A workshop report published on 2 October points the other way.
Acceptability would turn on intended use, impact, uncertainty and control strategy. Mandatory human review would give way to oversight proportionate to risk.
entries.catch: This is a workshop report, not adopted text. It carries no participant count and no timeline, so no date can be planned around.

glossary.definition: is the answer a model is trained and scored against.
measures whether accuracy differs between groups of patients.

entries.headline: Scraped labels made chest X ray models look fairer than they are
body: Automatically extracted labels missed 54 to 59 per cent of confirmed findings, and every fracture, in 4,376 expert checked images.
The misses were concentrated where models score lowest. Measured gaps between patient groups looked smaller under the scraped labels in 16 of 24 comparisons.
entries.catch: One public dataset, and an expert subset that was not built to be demographically balanced. The full text could not be read at source.

mechanism.pieces: The method takes a measured time course and estimates how fast it changes. It then asks which few entries from a menu of candidate formulas reproduce that rate.
mechanism.normally_wrong: Across the narrow range an oscillation visits, the curve for a gene switching on resembles the simple polynomial entries beside it. The fit cannot separate them.
mechanism.what_they_did: Known regulatory entries are removed from the menu. Their coefficients are pinned by a separate requirement, that the average rate of change over a bounded path is zero.
mechanism.numbers_mean: The 3 to 45 times is a gain in numerical stability, not in accuracy. That is the right quantity, because instability is the disease being treated.
mechanism.anchor: You supply the architecture and the method estimates its strengths. That is the hand off from a curated network to a quantitative one.

glossary.definition: fits with a penalty that pushes most coefficients to zero.
says how far small input errors are amplified. Lower is steadier.
is a paper posted before peer review.

entries.headline: A fix for why equation discovery cannot see gene regulation
body: The method improves the numerical stability of the fit by 3 to 45 times. On measured oscillation data it gave the lowest trajectory error of four methods.
On two synthetic systems it recovered the correct sparse structure. It still found every active term at 15 per cent noise, where two standard methods failed.
entries.catch: You must already know which regulatory terms exist, so this puts numbers on a hypothesised architecture. One real dataset and two textbook systems.
entries.simple: Scientists guess the equations behind a measured biological rhythm. For genes the guess is unstable, because one curve looks like another. This method pins part of it in advance.
entries.why: If you hold a curated map and a time course, this puts numbers on the edges without the fit collapsing.

glossary.definition: is a small group of cells still joined after gentle separation.
is a short DNA tag marking where a molecule came from.

entries.headline: A method keeps cells in small clumps, so sequencing can say which sat together
body: Tissue is broken only into clumps of under about 20 cells, and every cell in a clump is given one shared tag before full separation.
In a mixing control, 2 of 682 clumps held both species. In gut tissue the method read 6.5 times as many genes as one established spatial platform.
entries.catch: The authors say this captures a range from true contact to short range neighbourhood, not certified contact. Five tumour patients cannot carry the subtype claims.

mechanism.pieces: An agent calls tools that change outside systems. A fault injection is a deliberate failure placed mid run. Idempotency means repeating an operation has no further effect.
mechanism.normally_wrong: Most benchmarks score only whether the task finished. That mixes planning skill with recovery skill, and hides the half completed action.
mechanism.what_they_did: They ran matched pairs with the same random seed, once clean and once with a fault. They then tracked the state of the environment, not the agent's account.
mechanism.numbers_mean: The first number is what a vendor quotes. The second is what happens when something goes wrong, which in production is routine. The duplicate rate carries a direct cost.
mechanism.anchor: Test the failure path, not the happy path. Then make every action safe to repeat, because the agent will repeat it.

glossary.definition: is a language model that acts over several steps using tools.
means repeating an operation does not change the result again.
fixes the random choices so two runs can be compared fairly.

entries.headline: Agents finish 84 per cent of tasks and recover from 47 per cent of failures
body: A benchmark pairs 36 business workflows with 36 fault scenarios. Agents completed 83.54 per cent of clean tasks and recovered from 46.72 per cent of injected faults.
Retrying produced duplicate real world effects in 53.33 per cent of trials. After an action was committed, only verification plus a guard against repeats helped.
entries.catch: Only 36 scenarios, all simulated, and the abstract does not name the models tested.
entries.simple: Assistants that act on real systems were tested twice. Normally they finished most jobs. With a deliberate problem in the middle, they fixed fewer than half.
entries.why: Report the share of tasks that pass every run, and how many failures were silent. Those two numbers decide whether a human must check the work.

glossary.definition: is the step that weighs which inputs matter most.
is ordinary software imitating a quantum computer.

entries.headline: A quantum derived attention layer moved accuracy between genes rather than raising it
body: Across 29 cancer collections, more genes improved than worsened in 16 of them. On an independent collection about 2,000 genes improved and about 6,200 got worse.
Training ran on an ordinary computer simulating the circuit. Real hardware was used only to produce the matrices separately.
entries.catch: The model never ran on quantum hardware. Gains came in small collections while the independent test went backwards, and the obvious classical control is not reported.

glossary.definition: is how many people live outside their birth country at one time.
is a paper describing a dataset rather than testing a hypothesis.

entries.headline: A new open dataset estimates migration between every pair of countries since 1960
body: The dataset gives yearly flows between all countries from 1960 to 2024, split by sex. It comes from a migration organisation's data institute in Berlin.
Two stock series are reconciled, births and deaths are subtracted to get net flows, and a trained network splits net into gross.
entries.catch: These are modelled estimates, not counts. Sixty five years of history rest partly on a network trained on four recent years, and the authors say so.

glossary.definition: is a processor running ahead on a guess, then undoing it if wrong.
leaks information through timing or power rather than through output.

entries.headline: A speculative execution attack returns through just in time compilers
body: The attack leaks about 5.7 kilobytes a second on one processor family. Two affected projects shipped mitigations, and a browser maker is relying on process separation.
When a compiler rewrites code in place, the processor keeps stale predictions about where branches go. Freed code can then run speculatively and leak through timing.
entries.catch: It needs the attacker to run code on the machine already. The reported rates cover one chip vendor.
